title: Acyclicity of pulled-back injectives
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring. Use the small sites $X_{\Et}$ and $X_{\Proet}$ and the comparison geometric morphism $
u_X:X_{\Proet}	o X_{\Et}$. Let $\Lambda_{X,\Et}$ be the constant sheaf of rings and put $\Lambda_X=
u_X^{-1}\Lambda_{X,\Et}$. Here $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\Mod(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ mean sheaves of modules over these ring sheaves. The module inverse image $
u_X^*$ applies the abelian inverse image to the module and its scalar action, and $
u_{X,*}$ is the corresponding direct image. Right derived functors are computed by injective module resolutions.

If $I$ is an injective sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, then
$$
R^q
u_{X,*}
u_X^*I=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

proof.text: Use [def-weil-size-convention] to put the chosen small sites, their ring and module values, and covering index sets in one common universe. On $X$ and on each affine etale $W\to X$, both etale and pro-etale coefficient-module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Thus the injective-resolution computations and the ringed-site evaluation comparison used below apply with exactly their smallness and enough-injectives hypotheses.

Fix $q>0$ and put $M=
u_X^*I$. Part (1) of [det-pe-injective-acyclicity-reduction] says that $R^q
u_{X,*}M$ is the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^q(W_{\Proet},M|_W)$ on affine etale objects. It therefore suffices to prove that each of these module cohomology groups is zero. For such $W$, use only the first two assertions of part (2) of that node: $M|_W\cong
u_W^*(I|_W)$ and $I_W:=I|_W$ is injective on $W_{\Et}$. We do not take its vanishing assertion or its final consequence as an input.

Let $F_W=(I_W)_{ab}$ be the underlying abelian sheaf on $W_{\Et}$. Evaluation at the terminal object $W$ is additive and left exact: addition is sectionwise and kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Since $I_W$ is injective, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] gives $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(W,-)(I_W)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] on $W_{\Et}$ with ring sheaf $\Lambda_{W,\Et}$, object $W$, and module $I_W$. Its hypotheses were checked in step 1, and it identifies this zero group with $H^q(W_{\Et},F_W)$. This argument uses acyclicity of the underlying abelian sheaf, rather than assuming it is injective.

Apply [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] to the scheme $W$ and the abelian sheaf $F_W$. It gives $H^q(W_{\Proet},
u_W^{-1}F_W)\cong H^q(W_{\Et},F_W)=0$. By the definition of module inverse image in the statement, the underlying abelian sheaf of $
u_W^*I_W$ is exactly $
u_W^{-1}F_W$: applying inverse image to the scalar action changes no underlying abelian object. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] on $W_{\Proet}$ to its terminal object and the module $
u_W^*I_W$ over $\Lambda_W$. The same hypotheses from step 1 apply. Hence $H^q(W_{\Proet},
u_W^*I_W)=0$ in the module category. Neither comparison requires finite coefficients, torsion, constructibility, or affineness beyond the chosen affine test objects.

proof.text: The isomorphism of step 2 and the vanishing of step 4 give $H^q(W_{\Proet},M|_W)=0$ for every affine etale $W\to X$. The concluding implication of part (1) of [det-pe-injective-acyclicity-reduction] therefore gives $R^q\nu_{X,*}M=0$. Since $q>0$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion.

lean.note: Arbitrary discrete commutative coefficients, intrinsic ringed-site modules. The pro-etale ring is the actual inverse image of the constant etale ring; module inverse image uses the canonical ring unit and constructed module pullback on AsSmall models, followed by transport back. Vanishing is stated as H^q of direct image applied to EVERY injective module resolution, precisely the node's stated definition of R^q, using InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj.
